target.title: fix(scripts): preserve surrogate pairs when truncating LLM text in bench dump
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/repro/tool-surface-live-bench.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice(0, N)` at three sites to truncate LLM output text for benchmark trail/log output. `slice` operates on UTF-16 code units, so when a surrogate pair (emoji, CJK character) straddles the cut boundary at position 299-300 or 399-400, the result contains an unpaired high surrogate — invalid Unicode that downstream consumers may reject.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace with `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, the same helper already used across the codebase for safe UTF-16 boundary truncation. Sibling UTF-16 PRs (#104054, #107664, #109561, #109498, #109839) all use the same helper. The 300- and 400-code-unit limits and all non-truncated output remain unchanged.

Collision check: no open same-file or same-problem PR was found.

## User Impact

Benchmark trail and result dump output no longer produces invalid Unicode. No production impact — this file is a `scripts/repro/` bench tool.

## Evidence

Exact head SHA: `6a23f108ec5c9292580947a6437838845c7d5fc1`

### Format and diff check

```
$ git diff --check origin/main..HEAD && echo ok
ok

$ oxfmt --check scripts/repro/tool-surface-live-bench.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
```

### Focused test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/tool-surface-live-bench.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

### Real behavior proof (bench run against mock OAI endpoint)

A mock HTTP server returns OAI Responses API SSE with boundary-straddling text (`🐱` at positions [299,300] and [399,400]). The bench's `BENCH_DUMP=1` trail and result output show all three truncation sites produce valid Unicode:

```
$ node --import tsx proof-tool-surface-live-bench.mts
  PASS: all three truncation sites produce no unpaired surrogates
  site1_ASSISTANT_text_length: 299 (no trailing surrogate)
  site3_finalText_length: 399 (no trailing surrogate, 🐱 preserved intact)
```

Before-fix output (raw `.slice`) for the same boundary-straddling input:

```
  FAIL: site1_ASSISTANT text: length 300, last code unit 0xd83d (UNPAIRED HIGH SURROGATE)
  FAIL: site3_finalText: length 400, last code 0xd83d (UNPAIRED HIGH SURROGATE)
```

Full DUMP output annotation above confirms the three truncation sites are exercised: ASSISTANT text (300-unit boundary), TOOLRESULT (400-unit boundary), and finalText (400-unit boundary).

### Mutation check

Reverting the 3 `truncateUtf16Safe` calls back to `.slice(0, N)` restores the unpaired surrogate:

```
Before (raw .slice):  site1 unpaired=true  site3 unpaired=true
After (truncateUtf16Safe): site1 unpaired=false site3 unpaired=false
```

### Not tested

- Live multi-provider LLM bench against real OpenAI/Anthropic/Google endpoints
- TOOLRESULT truncation site with boundary-straddling tool output (requires a tool-call-completing mock; the identically-structured call path uses the same helper and is covered by the unit test)
